transcript.text:
Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Let's get it sorted. When a washing machine won't spin, the usual causes, most likely first, are: 1. It hasn't drained. Machines won't spin until the water has gone, so a blocked pump filter, a kinked drain hose or a struggling drain pump all show up as "won't spin".
2. The load is unbalanced. One heavy item (a bath mat, towels, a duvet) or a very small load makes the machine skip or cut the spin on purpose. That's normal behaviour, not a fault.
3. A setting. A no-spin, rinse-hold or very low spin option may have been selected.
4. A drive or mechanical fault (motor, brushes, belt or a speed sensor). This is less likely, and only worth considering once the above are ruled out. Checks that tell these apart: 1. Look in the drum when it stops. If there's water still in it, the problem is draining, not spinning, and the pump filter is the first (and often free) fix. If the drum is empty and the clothes are just wet, draining is fine and we look at the load or the drive.
2. Check the programme. Make sure the spin speed isn't set to 0 or "no spin" and that rinse hold isn't on, then run a spin-only programme.
3. Try a balanced load. If it was a single heavy item, add a few smaller things or spread the load out and run a spin again. If it spins fine then, it was just imbalance. If it still won't spin with a normal mixed load, that points to a fault.
4. Watch the drum during the wash. If it turns normally while washing (or rocks slowly back and forth as if trying to balance), the motor can move the drum. If it never turns at all, that points towards the drive. The most useful thing to know first: when it stops, is there still water in the drum? If there is, don't open the pump filter yet without a towel and a shallow tray ready, because a lot of water can come out.
no water in the drum, its empty. just a soaking wet bath mat in there, nothing else. no error code either

That's very useful, and it's good news. An empty drum means it has drained, so the pump and filter aren't the problem. The mat soaks up water and clings to one side of the drum. The machine senses the imbalance and deliberately skips the spin to protect itself. That's normal behaviour, not a fault, and no error code is shown for it. 1. Add a few medium items to the drum with the mat, such as two or three bath towels, and spread them evenly. Then run a rinse and spin or spin-only programme. If it spins properly, it was just imbalance and nothing is wrong.
2. If you don't want to add anything, take the mat out and run a spin-only programme with the drum empty. If it spins up fine empty, the machine is healthy and the mat was the cause.
3. While you're at it, check the spin speed isn't set to 0 or 'no spin' and that rinse hold is off. If it still won't spin with a balanced load, or with the drum completely empty, that would point to a genuine drive fault, such as the belt, carbon brushes or motor. Tell me what happens. It also helps to know whether the drum turns during the wash, or just sits still.
ok i did a rinse n spin with the mat plus a couple of towels and it spins fine, mat comes out damp not dripping. spin is on the normal 1000 setting too

That settles it. So the machine is healthy. It was skipping the spin on purpose because the soaked bath mat on its own was pulling the drum off balance. No part is needed. To stop it happening again, never wash a bath mat, rug or single heavy item on its own. Pair it with two or three towels or similar-weight items so the weight spreads around the drum. It would only be worth looking at again if it starts refusing to spin with normal mixed loads, or if it bangs and moves about violently when it does spin. Is there anything else I can help with?

candidates: Water not draining (blocked pump filter, hose or drain pump) so spin is blocked (high)
Unbalanced or awkward load (one heavy item, small load) so spin is skipped (high)
Drive or mechanical fault (motor, brushes, belt, sensor) if the drum is empty and it still won't spin with a normal load (medium)
Programme setting (no-spin, rinse hold or very low spin selected) (low)
